per_window.ps-ns: dynamic_in_window: at 298 K, pH 6.8 the free isolated N-domain has its lowest S2 in loops 30-33, 64, 106-108, 122-123 and the termini (R18092-J1, r1), with nanosecond internal motion at 30-31, 64 and 122-123 (1.05 ± 0.05 ns; J2, r1). Per-residue S2 values are in an unread supplement.
per_window.us-ms: dynamic_in_window (indirect): single-field model-free Rex at I45, D54-G57, K63, N67 and E134-A135 around helices alpha2 and alpha3 (J3, r1); no dispersion, rate or population.
per_window.slower_than_ms: unresolved (search_insufficient): no row gives a slow rate, and the method searches used the viral identity on the card (J8).
per_window.undetermined: Two resolved peak sets, minor 10-20% (about 5:1), placed by the authors at the interface of the beta-sheet core with helices alpha2 and alpha3 (J4, r2): slow on the chemical-shift timescale but no rate. Missing N86 and weak R65, E103, T133 amides are attributed to water exchange (J5, artefact_suspected). Crystal versus solution: remote loops 29-33, 61-64 and 101-105 differ, read as intrinsic (J6), while 115-123, 41-42 and 89-91 are likely construct effects (J7); both unresolved, structure_only. Not judged: r3 (RDC/NOE-restrained ensemble 2LLX, spread is not a motional amplitude); r5 and r6 (mouse full-length and C-domain eRF1 crystals bound to MoMLV RT or RNase H; other construct and partner, and r6 residues lie outside the entry).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Yes, without a rate: at 298 K, pH 6.8 in 10 mM sodium phosphate, the free isolated eRF1 N-domain (the entry construct with a His6 tag) shows a second peak set for several residues with a 10-20% minor conformer (about 5:1), proposed to reorient helices alpha2 and alpha3 around the NIKS loop, and single-field model-free Rex at I45, D54-G57, K63, N67 and E134-A135; no exchange rate is measured and the minor conformer is not shown to be the Rex process.
open_conflicts: Not a conflict but an open link: the Rex residues (J3) and the doubled-peak conformer (J4) both sit around helices alpha2 and alpha3, but the source does not show that they are one process (r1, r2).
questions_for_gina: The card's UniProt P03355 is the Moloney murine leukemia virus Gag-Pol polyprotein, not this sequence; the entry sequence is human eRF1 N-domain 1-142 plus LE (P62495), and the 2012 paper deposits its R1/R2/NOE under BMRB 18092. Should the entry be relabelled and the method searches rerun under human eRF1 names?
Should the 5:1 peak doubling count as an alternate apo state when no exchange cross-peaks or rate are reported and causes such as proline isomerization or sample heterogeneity were not tested?
protein_summary.buffer_note: All NMR rows (r1-r4) are one sample type: about 1 mM isolated N-domain with C-terminal His6 in 10 mM sodium phosphate, 25 mM NaCl, about 2 mM beta-mercaptoethanol, pH 6.8, 298 K; relaxation at 600 MHz only. This domain recognizes mRNA and no buffer-substitution control exists, so a phosphate effect is possible but not shown. Supporting Figs. S1, S4 and S5 (doubled-peak spectra, per-residue S2/Rex, model selection) were not readable. The source organism of the evidence is Homo sapiens (eRF1, UniProt P62495); the mouse eRF1 rows r5 and r6 are a sequence-identical homolog in other constructs. No deposition readback file exists for 18092. Second read flagged no row.
